stem:
The figure shows Nitya's garden plot: rectangle ABCD is $6\ \mathrm{cm}$ by $4\ \mathrm{cm}$, and right triangle AEB has base $6\ \mathrm{cm}$ and height $3\ \mathrm{cm}$ on top of the rectangle.

How should she find the area of the figure?

options.text: Add the rectangle area $6 \times 4$ and the triangle area $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 3$.
Use only the rectangle area $6 \times 4$, because the triangle sits on the rectangle.
The triangle area produces the rectangle area, so multiply those two part areas.
Any closed garden plot has area $6 \times 4$.

teacher.key_rationale: Partition into rectangle and triangle, then add part areas: 24 + 9 = 33. Omitting the triangle drops a part. Multiplying part areas reverses add-for-composite. Treating every closed shape as 6×4 over-scopes the rectangle rule.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote rectangle-triangle source into a labeled 6-by-4 rectangle with a height-3 triangle on top; stem refers to the figure.
